pages.text: The next day, {hero} and {pet} walked to Candy Village. The houses were made of cake, and the roofs were [[covered|with something all over the top]] in pink icing. The whole village smelled sweeter than a birthday party.

q.q: What were the roofs covered in?
q.explain: “The roofs were covered in pink icing.”

pages.text: In the market they met Mrs Toffee, the baker. She looked [[worried|unhappy because you think something bad may happen]]. “Someone took my best cake last night,” she said. “And I found this strange paper next to my oven.” It was the second page!

q.explain: “Someone took my best cake last night.”

pages.text: The page had a [[clue|something that helps you find an answer]] on it: “Follow the crumbs.” {hero} looked down. There was a line of tiny cake crumbs on the road. It went past the school and into the park.

q.q: What did the clue tell them to do?

pages.text: In the park they found a very small dragon. It was eating the cake. “Sorry!” it said. “I was so hungry.” Mrs Toffee [[laughed|made a happy sound because something was funny]]. “Next time, just ask! I'm going to bake you your own cake.” {hero} put the page in the book.

q.q: What is Mrs Toffee going to do?
q.explain: “I'm going to bake you your own cake.” — going to = a plan.

final.q: In the story, a “clue” is something that…
final.explain: A clue helps you find the answer to a mystery.

chapters.title: The Balloon Festival
chapters.focus: past simple · comparatives and superlatives · going to

pages.text: A week later, Candy Village had its Balloon Festival. Every child got a balloon, and the sky was full of colours. Mrs Toffee gave {hero} the biggest balloon of all. It was pink and as round as a [[melon|a big round fruit, green outside and sweet inside]].

q.explain: “Mrs Toffee gave {hero} the biggest balloon of all.”

notes.the little dragon: The dragon comes later in the story. “Mrs Toffee gave {hero} the biggest balloon of all.”
notes.a child from the school: Every child got a balloon, but {hero}'s came from Mrs Toffee.
notes.{pet}: {pet} didn't give it. “Mrs Toffee gave {hero} the biggest balloon of all.”

pages.text: Suddenly a strong wind came. The balloon [[slipped|moved out of your hand by accident]] out of {hero}'s hand and flew up into the tallest tree in the village, the old candy-cane tree. {hero} tried to climb it, but the trunk was too [[sticky|covered in something sweet that holds on to you]].

q.explain: “{hero} tried to climb it, but the trunk was too sticky.”

It was “the tallest tree in the village”, not a short one.
The wind was strong, but the story doesn't say it was cold. The problem was the sticky trunk.
The story doesn't say {pet} was scared. The trunk “was too sticky.”

pages.text: Then they heard a small voice. “I can help!” It was Crumb, the little dragon who ate the cake last week. Crumb was smaller than a cat, but his wings were stronger than they looked. He flew up, took the string in his [[claws|the sharp nails on an animal's foot]] and brought the balloon down.

q.q: What do we learn about Crumb's wings?
options: They were stronger than they looked.
They were bigger than a cat.
They were sticky like the tree.
They were too weak to fly up very high.
q.explain: “His wings were stronger than they looked.” (stronger than = comparing two things)

It was Crumb who was “smaller than a cat”. The story doesn't say how big his wings were.
The tree trunk was sticky, not Crumb's wings.
He flew up into the tallest tree, so his wings were strong, not weak.

pages.text: Everyone [[clapped|hit their hands together to show they liked something]]. “Thank you, Crumb!” said {hero}. “You're the bravest dragon in Candy Village.” Crumb's cheeks went pink. “Next year I'm going to fly in the festival too,” he said. “Can I have a balloon of my own?”

q.q: What is Crumb going to do next year?
q.explain: “Next year I'm going to fly in the festival too.” Going to = a plan.

notes.bake a balloon cake: Mrs Toffee is the baker. Crumb's plan is to “fly in the festival”.
notes.climb the candy tree: Crumb can fly, so he doesn't need to climb. His plan is to “fly in the festival”.
notes.eat Mrs Toffee's cake: That happened last week, in the cake story. Next year he's going to “fly in the festival”.

final.q: In the story, the balloon “slipped”. That means it…
options: moved out of a hand by accident
was tied to a tall tree on purpose
final.explain: Slipped = moved out of {hero}'s hand by accident, because of the wind.

notes.was given to a friend: Nobody gave it away. The wind made it slip out of {hero}'s hand.
notes.popped with a loud bang: It didn't pop. It flew into the tree, and Crumb brought it down.
notes.was tied to a tall tree on purpose: Slipping is an accident, not something you do on purpose.

chapters.title: Crumb's Tiny Bakery
chapters.focus: past simple · comparatives and superlatives · going to

pages.text: After the Balloon Festival, Crumb wanted to say thank you. He opened the smallest bakery in Candy Village, right next to Mrs Toffee's shop. The door was shorter than a child, and the oven was the [[cosiest|warm and comfortable]] little oven anyone had ever seen.

q.q: Why did Crumb open a bakery?
options: to climb the candy tree again
q.explain: “Crumb wanted to say thank you. He opened the smallest bakery…”

notes.to win a balloon race: The balloon race was last week. This week he opened a bakery to say thank you.
notes.to hide from Mrs Toffee: His shop was “right next to Mrs Toffee's shop”, not a hiding place.
notes.to climb the candy tree again: Climbing the sticky tree was in the festival story. Now he is baking.

pages.text: On the first morning Crumb baked jam tarts. They were sweeter than honey and smaller than a coin. Children [[queued|stood in a line waiting for your turn]] outside the tiny door. “I'm going to bake something new every day,” Crumb said proudly.

q.q: What is Crumb going to do every day?
options: fly higher than the candy tree
q.explain: “I'm going to bake something new every day.” Going to = a plan.

notes.fly higher than the candy tree: Flying was his festival plan. His new plan is to “bake something new every day”.
notes.close the bakery at noon: The story doesn't say he will close at noon. He plans to bake something new.
notes.give away all the balloons: Balloons were last week. Now he plans to bake something new every day.

pages.text: Then a problem came. Crumb's claws were stronger than a spoon, and he [[squashed|pressed something so it became flat]] the first tray of tarts by accident. The tarts looked flatter than pancakes. Crumb's cheeks went pink. “Oh no. These are the messiest tarts in the village!”

q.q: What happened to the first tray of tarts?
options: The wind blew them into a tree.
A child hid them under the door.
q.explain: “He squashed the first tray of tarts by accident.”

Mrs Toffee has her own shop next door. Crumb squashed the tarts.
The wind was in the balloon story. Here, Crumb's claws squashed the tarts.
Children queued outside. Nobody hid the tarts; Crumb squashed them.

pages.text: {hero} and {pet} knocked on the little door. “We can help!” said {hero}. Together they cut the flat tarts into star shapes. The children [[clapped|hit their hands together to show they liked something]]. “These are the prettiest tarts of all,” said Mrs Toffee. Crumb smiled. “Tomorrow I'm going to use a softer spoon,” he laughed.

q.q: How did they fix the squashed tarts?
options: They cut them into star shapes.
They baked a bigger cake instead.
They threw them into the oven again.
They gave each child a balloon.
q.explain: “Together they cut the flat tarts into star shapes.”

They kept the tarts and reshaped them. Nobody baked a bigger cake.
Putting them back in the oven wouldn't make stars. They cut star shapes.
Balloons were last chapter. This time they cut the tarts into stars.

options: stood in a line waiting for their turn
ran as fast as they could
final.explain: Queued = stood in a line, waiting, like the children outside Crumb's door.

notes.ran as fast as they could: Queuing is waiting in a line, not running.
notes.hid under a tiny table: Nobody hid. The children stood outside the door.
